The survey crew counted nests along the northern shingle before the tide came in. Wind speed stayed below ten knots, which kept the grass short and the gravel dry. Rangers logged each sighting with a position fix, a species code and a short comment. Spare batteries, leg rings and a waterproof notebook travelled in the same crate. By evening the boat had returned twice, and the harbour master closed the log at 16:45. Nothing in the data suggested a decline; density was highest near the old lighthouse.
